title: On Casimir force between two real metallic plates
abstract: The corrections to Casimir pressure (force) on two plates of real metal described by the dielectric constant of the Drude, Drude-Lorentz, Drude-Smith and plasma models at the finite temperature and conductivity are considered. We consider the contour integral lost in the Lifshitz formula and discuss inconsistencies for the corrections to the Casimir force given in the literature. Numerical and analytical results in the near and far zones are presented. The two first-order correction obtained due to the actual dielectric constant of the metal coincided with the literature data.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the Casimir force between real metal plates by incorporating finite temperature and conductivity effects using advanced dielectric models. The authors critically analyze existing literature formulas, demonstrating mathematical inconsistencies that necessitate including dissipation terms for physically accurate results. It provides a detailed comparison of various physical regimes and material approximations.
main_problem: The paper investigates corrections to the Casimir force between two real metallic plates, accounting for finite temperature and conductivity effects.
main_result: The authors show that several published formulas for the correction terms are inconsistent due to mathematical divergences, requiring the inclusion of dissipation ($\propto \epsilon''(\omega)$) in the frequency integral for consistency.
method: The analysis relies on the Lifshitz formula, involving complex contour integration over frequency and wave vector, comparing results derived from various dielectric models (Drude, Plasma, etc.).
model_or_system: The system is two parallel metallic plates separated by a distance $d$. The material response is modeled using several dielectric functions ($\epsilon(\omega)$), including the Drude model, which captures frequency-dependent conductivity and temperature effects.
key_observables: Casimir pressure ($P$) and force density ($F$), showing dependence on separation distance ($d$) and temperature ($T$).
important_parameters: Separation distance $d$, Temperature $T$ (e.g., 5 K to 900 K), plasma frequency ($\omega_p$), collision frequency ($\omega_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis critically examines the mathematical consistency of existing literature formulas, particularly regarding how dissipation terms are handled in the integration process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the external Casimir pressure $P$ for various conditions: dependence on separation distance ($d$) and temperature ($T$), and comparison between different material models (Plasma vs. Drude-Smith).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical framework using the Lifshitz formula, comparing results from multiple dielectric models across different physical regimes (near/far zones), and rigorously analyzing mathematical inconsistencies in prior literature.
why_interesting: While focused on electrodynamics, the rigorous treatment of boundary conditions, dissipation ($\epsilon''$), and temperature corrections to vacuum forces touches upon open quantum system dynamics where environmental coupling is crucial for energy renormalization.
